topic: In Event of Moon Disaster: the speech written in case Apollo 11's crew could not return

facts.claim: A memo dated July 18, 1969, To: H. R. Haldeman, From: Bill Safire, titled 'IN EVENT OF MOON DISASTER:'
facts.source: The memo itself, page 1: National Archives Catalog NAID 6922351 (Nixon Library, H. R. Haldeman's Files), access and use 'Unrestricted'. https://catalog.archives.gov/id/6922351

facts.claim: Quote: 'Fate has ordained that the men who went to the moon to explore in peace will stay on the moon to rest in peace.'
The speech names Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin
'PRIOR TO THE PRESIDENT'S STATEMENT: The President should telephone each of the widows-to-be.'

'AFTER THE PRESIDENT'S STATEMENT, AT THE POINT WHEN NASA ENDS COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE MEN: A clergyman should adopt the same procedure as a burial at sea, commending their souls to "the deepest of the deep," concluding with the Lord's Prayer.'
Last line: 'some corner of another world that is forever mankind.'
William Safire was a speechwriter (NARA titles it 'Memorandum from Speechwriter William Safire to President Nixon')
Apollo 11 launched July 16, 1969, 9:32 a.m. EDT, Launch Pad 39A
Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility; Armstrong and Aldrin spent 21 hours, 36 minutes on the Moon's surface
The ascent stage engine fired at 124 hours, 22 minutes into the mission (July 21, 1969)
facts.status: verified (date computed from launch time + mission elapsed time)

facts.source: NASA, '55 Years Ago: Apollo 11's One Small Step, One Giant Leap' (nasa.gov)

not_used.why: not checked against a NASA source today; left out

people: Real people appear only in NASA's own photographs and TV footage (public domain, credited). No AI faces, no voice imitation of Nixon (the speech is shown as a document, never performed).
